core.title: Tag every issue-body dependency entry as prereq, merged, sibling, or parallel
core.given: An issue body has a Dependencies section containing '#N' references to other issues (dependency entries), whether new or already present
core.when: That issue body is authored, edited, reviewed, or validated
core.then: Every '#N' dependency entry must carry a trailing classification tag that is exactly one of: prereq, merged, sibling, or parallel.
prefer: Put the classification as a trailing marker on each '#N' entry

Use prereq for work that must merge before this issue can proceed, and merged for a prereq that has already landed. Use sibling or parallel for related work that runs alongside this issue and is not waited on; the convention does not distinguish sibling from parallel, so either tag satisfies the rule for such work.
When an existing issue body has untagged or wrongly tagged entries, fix the tags on those entries
avoid: Leaving any '#N' entry untagged, or using a tag other than prereq/merged/sibling/parallel
Dropping or moving real dependencies out of the Dependencies section just to avoid having to classify them
core.why: Classifying each dependency prevents the session-template merge-wait loop from hanging on sibling or parallel work.
evidence: The stack's issue-body dependency-classification check passes for the issue body
Each '#N' reference in the Dependencies section carries a trailing marker that is exactly one of prereq, merged, sibling, or parallel
verification: Scope: the unit checked is the dependency entry — an '#N' reference in the Dependencies section of an issue body. '#N' references outside the Dependencies section are not in scope for this rule.
classification_tag: a trailing marker on the entry. The allowed set is closed — {prereq, merged, sibling, parallel} — and the check reports both missing and invalid tags.
Disposition: advisory, severity 2 — findings are reported but are not blocking. Suppressions are allowed only until this rule's suppression deadline (2026-12-31).

values: issue-body dependency entry with a missing or invalid classification tag

fires: A new issue body has a Dependencies section that lists one or more '#N' references
A '#N' entry is added to, or changed in, the Dependencies section of an existing issue body
An existing issue body is reviewed or validated and its Dependencies section has '#N' entries, even when nobody edits it
A '#N' entry in a Dependencies section has no trailing tag
A '#N' entry in a Dependencies section has a trailing marker that is not exactly one of prereq, merged, sibling, or parallel
doesNotFire: '#N' references that appear outside the Dependencies section, e.g. in the narrative or graph-context sections
An issue body that has no Dependencies section or no '#N' entries in it
Code, tests, or docs that are not issue bodies

bunOnly.text: Validator test_issue_deps_have_classification_tags passes for the issue body
bunOnly.reason: The validator/finding id of this one rule is a realization detail; the core names the check generically in core.evidence[0], and instantiating that with this id restores the exact Bun evidence.

bunOnly.text: finding values: ["test_issue_deps_have_classification_tags"] — validator finding for a '#N' entry in a Dependencies section whose tag is missing or is not one of prereq/merged/sibling/parallel
bunOnly.reason: The finding id of this rule's validator is a realization detail; the core keeps the same fact slot with a generic description of the finding, and this id restores the exact Bun value.

neutralityNotes: This rule constrains issue-body (tracker) content rather than repository code, so it is almost entirely stack-neutral and needs nothing from a structure profile: profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. The '#N' reference notation, the 'Dependencies' section heading, the narrative/graph-context section names, and the four tags belong to the shared issue-body/session template, not to any stack, so they are kept in the core text; the closed profile vocabulary covers repository structure only and has no tracker-syntax keys, which is correct here because the core needs none. The only realization details are this rule's validator/finding id (bunOnly); the term ids dependency_entry and classification_tag come from the canonical source and are stack-neutral, so they are retained in core.verification. Per-rule severity (2), disposition (advisory, non-blocking), and the 2026-12-31 suppression deadline are rule metadata and live in core.verification, not in a profile.
